rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes alloying an elemental Cr coating with Al, whereas the target paper uses a TiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coating with varying Al content. This represents a different kind of intervention (composition change in a different alloy system).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions normal subcritical-water operation (~350°C) and accident-relevant steam up to ~1200°C, while the target paper tests isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C. The broad high-temperature steam regime is shared, but the specific temperatures and the inclusion of subcritical-water conditions differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes an Al-rich interlayer/oxide at the coating/substrate interface acting as a diffusion barrier to Cr-Zr interdiffusion. The target paper's mechanism involves a surface Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite oxide layer suppressing oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing detrimental intermetallics. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced Cr-Zr interdiffusion and improved integrity relative to an elemental Cr coating. The target paper predicts and observes an optimum Al content (~10 at.%) minimizing oxidation rate and oxygen penetration, with higher Al reversing the benefit. The predicted property (interdiffusion vs. oxidation) and the comparison baseline differ.
